title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 40
paragraphs: At this the Ephors and the Senate deliberated together and put this proposal to Anaxandrides: “Since then we see that you are firmly attached to the wife you now have, agree to do this, and do not set yourself against it—lest the Spartans take some counsel concerning you otherwise than you would wish. We do not ask you to put away the wife you have; rather, continue to give her everything you give her now, and at the same time take into your house another wife besides this one, to bear you children.” When they spoke to him in this way, Anaxandrides consented, and so he had two wives—a thing by no means in keeping with Spartan custom.
